mainTopic: Which foods and which kinds of מצה are valid for the מצוה of מצה: ביכורים versus מעשר שני, the אונן dispute, and what ״לחם עוני״ excludes.
overview: This amud asks which foods can be used for the מצוה of מצה. The גמרא first shows that רבי עקיבא retracted an earlier derivation. A ברייתא then gives his final view: ביכורים are excluded by ״בכל מושבותיכם״, while מעשר שני is included by ״מצות״ ״מצות״. The difference is that מעשר שני can become permitted outside ירושלים through redemption, as רבי אליעזר teaches, while ביכורים never can. The גמרא then explains why רבי יוסי הגלילי does not exclude ביכורים with ״לחם עוני״. He holds like רבי שמעון that an אונן may eat ביכורים, and this leads into the dispute between רבי שמעון and the רבנן. Next, a ברייתא teaches that ״לחם עוני״ rules out boiled מצה and large cakes (אשישה), but not fine flour. The גמרא proves from a פסוק about דוד המלך that אשישה is something important, and records a disagreement over what the word means. The amud ends with בית שמאי forbidding thick bread on פסח, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Worry: maybe wheat and barley are excluded entirely
steps.stepSummary: Continuing רבי עקיבא's line of reasoning, one might think to exclude wheat and barley from מצה, since ביכורים are brought from those grains.
steps.simpleTranslation: I would exclude wheat and barley, since ביכורים are brought from their species.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues a hypothetical from the previous section. It raises a fear that the reasoning used so far would wrongly disqualify wheat and barley from being used for מצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's derivation disqualified certain foods from מצה. If we follow that logic too far, wheat and barley themselves look suspect, because those are the species that ביכורים come from. This is a problem, since wheat and barley are the classic grains for מצה. So the גמרא needs a source to block this conclusion.

keyTerms.meaning: First fruits brought to the בית המקדש and eaten in ירושלים
In their species / of their kind

phrases.english: I would exclude wheat and barley
phrases.notes: Continues an 'I might have thought' line earlier.

phrases.english: since among their species there are first fruits.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹצִיא חִיטִּין וּשְׂעוֹרִין שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּמִינָן בִּיכּוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the derivation earlier.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the derivation excludes things linked to ביכורים, it would disqualify wheat and barley altogether.

steps.title: The repeated word ״מצות״ widens the law
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק repeats ״מצות״ to include, so wheat and barley are not excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says ״מצות״, ״מצות״, which comes to include.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the worry. The repetition of the word ״מצות״ in the תורה is a רִיבּוּי, an extra word that comes to include more cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word ״מצות״ teaches that we should not narrow which grains count for מצה. So wheat and barley remain fully valid, even though ביכורים come from those species.

keyTerms.meaning: Matzos (plural), the repeated word in the פסוק

phrases.english: The verse states: "matzot", "matzot" — it included.
phrases.notes: The word appears more than once (דברים טז:ג, ח); the repetition comes to include.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the worry of step 1.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Wheat and barley might be excluded because ביכורים come from them.

steps.title: If the word includes, then include first fruits too
steps.stepSummary: If ״מצות״ ״מצות״ widens the law, it should include even actual ביכורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: If ״מצות״ ״מצות״ comes to include, then ביכורים should be included as well!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. A wide inclusion seems to prove too much.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A general ריבוי has no built-in limit. If it includes everything, then even מצה made from real ביכורים should count. That would undercut רבי עקיבא's original exclusions.

phrases.english: If "matzot", "matzot" included,
then even first fruits as well!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 2.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An open-ended inclusion should also include ביכורים, which contradicts רבי עקיבא's position.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא changed his mind
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי עקיבא retracted his earlier position.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא retracted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא does not defend the old derivation. It says רבי עקיבא himself withdrew it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's final view matches the ברייתא brought next. ביכורים are excluded for a different reason, ״בכל מושבותיכם״. מעשר שני is included by ״מצות״ ״מצות״. So the challenge in step 3 no longer applies.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא whose view is being discussed

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי עקיבא now allows ביכורים for מצה. He withdrew his earlier derivation, but he still excludes ביכורים, now through ״בכל מושבותיכם״.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva retracted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 3 by withdrawing the original position.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא's earlier derivation stands and faces the challenge.
steps.terutzMaskana: He retracted and adopted the ברייתא's approach.

steps.title: ברייתא: first fruits are excluded by 'in all your dwellings'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא excludes ביכורים because valid מצה must be food that can be eaten everywhere, and ביכורים may be eaten only in ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As taught in a ברייתא: I might think a person can fulfill his obligation with ביכורים. The פסוק says ״בכל מושבותיכם תאכלו מצות״ — מצה that can be eaten in all dwelling places. This excludes ביכורים, which can be eaten only in ירושלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that shows רבי עקיבא's new position. This first half explains why ביכורים are not valid for מצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words ״בכל מושבותיכם״ (in all your dwellings) set a requirement. The מצה must be the kind of food that can be eaten anywhere. ביכורים are limited to ירושלים, so they fail this test.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: יָכוֹל יֵצֵא אָדָם יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ בְּבִיכּוּרִים,
phrases.english: As it was taught: I might think a person fulfills his obligation with first fruits,
the verse states: "In all your dwellings you shall eat matzot"
— matza that is eaten in all dwellings,

phrases.aramaic: יָצְאוּ בִּיכּוּרִים שֶׁאֵינָן נֶאֱכָלִין בְּכׇל מוֹשָׁבוֹת
phrases.english: excluding first fruits, which are not eaten in all dwellings
but only in Jerusalem.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: יָכוֹל יֵצֵא אָדָם יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ בְּבִיכּוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the retraction by showing the source of the new view.

steps.title: ברייתא: second tithe is included by 'matzot, matzot'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: one might also exclude מעשר שני, but ״מצות״ ״מצות״ includes it.
steps.simpleTranslation: I might think I should also exclude מעשר שני. The פסוק says ״מצות״, ״מצות״, which includes.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא's second half uses the ריבוי of ״מצות״ ״מצות״ to include מעשר שני, which is also normally eaten only in ירושלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר שני looks like ביכורים, since both are eaten in ירושלים. So one might think it is excluded too. The ריבוי of ״מצות״ ״מצות״ includes it. Including מעשר שני was always רבי עקיבא's view. What is new is that this ברייתא excludes ביכורים through ״בכל מושבותיכם״, and step 11 uses that to prove he retracted.

keyTerms.meaning: Second tithe, eaten in ירושלים or redeemed for money

steps.whatToRemember: Final rule: מצה from ביכורים is invalid (because of ״בכל מושבותיכם״). מצה from מעשר שני is valid (because of ״מצות״ ״מצות״).

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל שֶׁאֲנִי מוֹצִיא אַף מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי,
phrases.english: I might think that I also exclude second tithe,
the verse states: "matzot", "matzot" — it included.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל שֶׁאֲנִי מוֹצִיא אַף מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מעשר שני is valid for מצה because of the ריבוי.

steps.title: Why include second tithe and not first fruits?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks what reason we have to apply the inclusion to מעשר שני rather than to ביכורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did you see that made you include מעשר שני and exclude ביכורים?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a clarifying question. Both foods are limited to ירושלים, so why does each go in a different direction?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two competing sources, an exclusion (״בכל מושבותיכם״) and an inclusion (״מצות״ ״מצות״). We need a logical reason to decide which food fits which source. The next step supplies that reason.

keyTerms.meaning: What did you see / what reason do you have

phrases.english: And what did you see to include second tithe
and to exclude first fruits?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה רָאִיתָ לְרַבּוֹת מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי וּלְהוֹצִיא בִּיכּוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how steps 5 and 6 divide the two cases.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The distinguishing factor between מעשר שני and ביכורים.

steps.title: Second tithe can become permitted everywhere; first fruits never can
steps.stepSummary: מעשר שני has a way to become permitted outside ירושלים, following רבי אליעזר. ביכורים have no such way.
steps.simpleTranslation: I include מעשר שני, which can become permitted in all dwelling places, as רבי אליעזר teaches. I exclude ביכורים, which have no way to become permitted in all dwelling places.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question. It gives the reason why מעשר שני is included and ביכורים are excluded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר שני can be redeemed. Once redeemed, the food loses its holiness and can be eaten anywhere. So it partly meets the ״בכל מושבותיכם״ standard. ביכורים can never leave ירושלים, so they fail completely.

keyTerms.meaning: A permitted status / a way to be allowed

steps.whyThisMatters: The test is not whether a food is eaten everywhere right now. It is whether it has any possible route to being permitted everywhere.

phrases.english: I include second tithe
which has a permitted state in all dwellings,
in accordance with Rabbi (Eliezer),
and I exclude first fruits
which have no permitted state in all dwellings.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְרַבֶּה אֲנִי מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ הֶיתֵּר בְּכׇל מוֹשָׁבוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מעשר שני can be redeemed and then eaten anywhere; ביכורים never can.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's source: impure second tithe is redeemed even in Jerusalem
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר derives from ״כי לא תוכל שאתו״ that impure מעשר שני may be redeemed even inside ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי אליעזר said: From where do we know that מעשר שני that became impure may be redeemed even in ירושלים? The פסוק says ״כי לא תוכל שאתו״.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source behind 'כדרבי אליעזר'. It shows how מעשר שני can become permitted everywhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, once מעשר שני is inside ירושלים, it cannot be redeemed. רבי אליעזר teaches that if it became טמא, it may be redeemed even there. The redeemed food can then be eaten anywhere. He reads this from the words ״כי לא תוכל שאתו״, and the גמרא will explain that reading next.

keyTerms.meaning: Carrying it / bearing it (to be expounded)

phrases.english: As Rabbi (Eliezer) said:
From where is it derived regarding second tithe that became impure,
that one redeems it even in Jerusalem?
The verse states: "For you are not able to carry it."
phrases.notes: דברים יד:כד. The גמרא will explain how this word refers to impure produce.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי (אֱלִיעֶזֶר): מִנְיָן לְמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי שֶׁנִּטְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for 'כדרבי אליעזר' in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that מעשר שני has a היתר in all dwellings
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אליעזר's reading of ״כי לא תוכל שאתו״

steps.title: The word for carrying actually means eating
steps.stepSummary: The word ״שאת״ in the פסוק means eating. This is proven from ״וישא משאת מאת פניו״, where ״משאת״ means food portions.
steps.simpleTranslation: And ״שאת״ means only eating, as it says: 'And he took portions from before him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבי אליעזר's proof from Step 9. It shows that ״כי לא תוכל שאתו״ means 'when you cannot eat it.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once ״שאתו״ means 'eat it,' the פסוק covers מעשר שני that is inside ירושלים but cannot be eaten because it became impure. That מעשר שני may be redeemed and the money spent elsewhere. So מעשר שני does have a way to be permitted outside ירושלים, which is why it counts as food 'in all your dwellings.'

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'carrying,' here explained to mean eating
Portions of food (from the story of יוסף and his brothers)
As it is stated (introduces a פסוק as proof)

phrases.english: And 'carrying' means nothing other than eating
as it is stated:
'And he took portions from before him' (Bereishis 43:34)
phrases.notes: Here ״משאת״ clearly refers to portions of food, so the root נשא can relate to eating.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי אליעזר's derivation from Step 9 by defining the key word ״שאתו״.
steps.raayaObject: That ״שאתו״ in ״כי לא תוכל שאתו״ means 'eat it,' so impure מעשר שני in ירושלים can be redeemed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק ״וישא משאת מאת פניו״ (בראשית מג:לד)

steps.title: רבי עקיבא must have changed his mind
steps.stepSummary: Only רבי עקיבא holds that one fulfills the מצוה of מצה with מעשר שני. Since this ברייתא follows that view and still excludes ביכורים from ״בכל מושבותיכם״, רבי עקיבא must have retracted and accepted this derivation.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whom have you heard say that one fulfills his obligation with מעשר שני? רבי עקיבא. And here he excludes ביכורים from 'in all your dwellings.' Learn from this that he retracted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who wrote the ברייתא and answers right away: רבי עקיבא. It then draws a conclusion about his position.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי עקיבא excluded ביכורים through a different derivation, the one that led to the worry about wheat and barley in step 1. He did not use ״בכל מושבותיכם״. This ברייתא lets you use מעשר שני, which is his view, yet it excludes ביכורים with ״בכל מושבותיכם״. That shows he dropped his old derivation and accepted this one.

keyTerms.meaning: Whom have you heard say this? (a formula for identifying a view's author)
One fulfills his obligation with it

steps.whyThisMatters: It matches the anonymous ברייתא to a known תנא. That match explains why ביכורים are excluded even according to the view that allows מעשר שני.

phrases.english: Whom have you heard who says
that one fulfills his obligation with second tithe?
Rabbi Akiva.
And yet he excludes first fruits
from 'in all your dwellings.'
Learn from this that he retracted.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן שָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ דְּאָמַר בְּמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי נָפֵיק בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the ברייתא's logic is complete, the גמרא identifies its author and draws a conclusion about his view.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא, who retracted and accepted the derivation of ״בכל מושבותיכם״ to exclude ביכורים.

steps.title: Why doesn't רבי יוסי הגלילי use ״לחם עוני״?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי learns from ״לחם עוני״ that מצה must be food an אונן may eat. Since ביכורים are eaten only with joy, ״לחם עוני״ should already exclude them, so why does he need ״בכל מושבותיכם״?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי הגלילי: let him derive it from 'bread of affliction,' meaning food that may be eaten in mourning. That excludes this, which is eaten only in joy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי הגלילי. He seems to have an extra source for excluding ביכורים that he does not need.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי reads ״לחם עוני״ as ״לחם אוני״: bread that may be eaten by a mourner (אונן). He used this to exclude מעשר שני, which may be eaten only in joy. Since ביכורים also require joy, the same exclusion should cover them, making ״בכל מושבותיכם״ unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him derive it from (a challenge that another source already covers this)
Bread of affliction, read here as 'bread of mourning'
Acute mourning / a mourner on the day a close relative died
Joy, a required state for eating certain holy foods

steps.confusionAlert: ״עוני״ is read with an א, as ״אוני״ (mourning), not just 'poverty.' This wordplay is the whole basis of the challenge.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,
let him derive it from 'bread of affliction'
that which is eaten in acute mourning,

phrases.aramaic: יָצָא זֶה שֶׁאֵין נֶאֱכָל אֶלָּא בְּשִׂמְחָה?
phrases.english: excluding this, which is eaten only in joy?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי תִּיפּוֹק לֵיהּ מִ״לֶּחֶם עוֹנִי״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי עקיבא to רבי יוסי הגלילי and questions why he needs ״בכל מושבותיכם״ for ביכורים.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי הגלילי's use of ״בכל מושבותיכם״ to exclude ביכורים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His own source, ״לחם עוני″, already excludes foods eaten only in joy. Since ביכורים are such a food, the second source seems unnecessary.

steps.title: He holds like רבי שמעון that a mourner may eat first fruits
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי follows רבי שמעון, who permits an אונן to eat ביכורים. So ״לחם עוני״ does not exclude ביכורים, and ״בכל מושבותיכם״ is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like רבי שמעון. As it was taught: ביכורים are forbidden to an אונן, and רבי שמעון permits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. According to רבי שמעון, ביכורים are not limited to joy-only eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The exclusion from ״לחם עוני״ removes only foods a mourner may not eat. רבי שמעון rules that an אונן may eat ביכורים, so they pass the ״לחם עוני״ test. Therefore רבי יוסי הגלילי still needs ״בכל מושבותיכם״ to exclude them, since they may be eaten only in ירושלים.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: There are two separate tests for מצה. Under ״לחם עוני״, a mourner must be allowed to eat it. Under ״בכל מושבותיכם״, it must be edible everywhere. For רבי יוסי הגלילי, ביכורים pass the first test (following רבי שמעון) but fail the second.

phrases.english: He holds in accordance with Rabbi Shimon.
As it was taught in a baraita:
First fruits are forbidden to an acute mourner,
and Rabbi Shimon permits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the challenge of Step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the תנא to a specific view (רבי שמעון) that removes the premise of the challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ביכורים are eaten only in joy and are forbidden to an אונן, so ״לחם עוני״ should exclude them.
steps.terutzMaskana: Following רבי שמעון, an אונן may eat ביכורים, so ״לחם עוני״ does not exclude them, and ״בכל מושבותיכם״ is needed.

steps.title: What is the source for the רבנן's view?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the רבנן, who forbid an אונן to eat ביכורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the רבנן forbid an אונן to eat ביכורים. This question sets up the next step, where the source is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 said that רבי שמעון permits an אונן to eat ביכורים. That means the רבנן disagree with him. The גמרא now wants to see the reasoning behind each side.

phrases.english: What is the reason of the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: The רבנן hold that an אונן may not eat ביכורים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 13 mentioned the dispute about whether an אונן may eat ביכורים. This step asks for the reasoning behind the רבנן's side.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for forbidding ביכורים to an אונן.

steps.title: First fruits are compared to tithe
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק lists ביכורים together with מעשר. Since מעשר is forbidden to an אונן, ביכורים are forbidden too.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: "You may not eat within your gates" (the list includes "the offering of your hand"). The Master said: "the offering of your hand" means ביכורים. So ביכורים are compared to מעשר. Just as מעשר is forbidden to an אונן, so too ביכורים are forbidden to an אונן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the רבנן's source. One פסוק lists ביכורים together with מעשר, so the two share the same law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase "תרומת ידך" in the list is understood to mean ביכורים. Because ביכורים and מעשר are listed in the same פסוק, this creates a הקש, a comparison that links their laws. The Torah says outright that מעשר is forbidden to an אונן, so the same rule carries over to ביכורים.

keyTerms.meaning: The offering of your hand, here meaning ביכורים
Was compared by a הקש (linked in the same verse)
A mourner on the day a close relative dies, before burial
First fruits brought to the בית המקדש

steps.confusionAlert: Here the words "תרומת ידך" do NOT mean ordinary תרומה. In this פסוק they mean ביכורים.

phrases.english: As it is written: "You may not eat within your gates"
phrases.notes: The verse goes on to list מעשר, firstborn animals, vows, and "the offering of your hand".

phrases.english: And the Master said: "the offering of your hand"
these are the first fruits,
for first fruits are compared to tithe:
phrases.notes: They are compared because they appear in the same verse.

phrases.english: just as tithe is forbidden to an acute mourner,
phrases.notes: The Torah states this explicitly about מעשר.

phrases.english: so too first fruits are forbidden to an acute mourner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A הקש between ביכורים and מעשר, so the prohibition on an אונן carries over from מעשר to ביכורים.

steps.title: רבי שמעון compares first fruits to תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון points out that the Torah calls ביכורים "תרומה". Since תרומה is permitted to an אונן, so are ביכורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון says: the Torah called them "תרומה". So they are like תרומה. Just as תרומה is permitted to an אונן, so too ביכורים are permitted to an אונן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי שמעון's side. He focuses on the word "תרומה" in the same phrase and compares ביכורים to תרומה instead of to מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides use the same words, "תרומת ידך". The רבנן look at the list the words appear in, which links ביכורים to מעשר. רבי שמעון looks at the name the Torah chose, "תרומה", which links ביכורים to תרומה. Since תרומה is permitted to an אונן, he permits ביכורים too.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One (the Torah) called them
The priestly gift of produce, which an אונן may eat

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon says:
The Merciful One called them "terumah".
phrases.notes: This refers to the words "תרומת ידך".

phrases.english: So they are like terumah: just as terumah is permitted to an acute mourner,
so too first fruits are permitted to an acute mourner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to the רבנן's reasoning in step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ביכורים are called תרומה, so they share תרומה's law, which permits them to an אונן.

steps.title: But joy is written about first fruits
steps.stepSummary: Even without the הקש, the Torah writes "ושמחת" about ביכורים. An אונן cannot be joyful, so how can רבי שמעון permit him to eat them?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון: even if he does not accept the הקש, at least joy is written about ביכורים, as it says "And you shall rejoice in all the good". So how can an אונן eat them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון. Even if he rejects the comparison to מעשר, the Torah connects ביכורים with joy, and a mourner is not in a state of joy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge does not depend on the הקש at all. It uses a separate פסוק that mentions שמחה with ביכורים. If ביכורים must be eaten with joy, an אונן should be excluded no matter how we compare ביכורים to other gifts.

keyTerms.meaning: A comparison between two laws listed together in a verse

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, נְהִי דְּהֶיקֵּישׁ לֵית לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon: granted that he does not hold of the comparison,
phrases.notes: This refers to the comparison to מעשר from step 15.

phrases.english: still, joy is at least written about them,
as it is written: "And you shall rejoice in all the good"?
phrases.notes: This verse appears in the ביכורים passage (דברים כו:יא).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, נְהִי דְּהֶיקֵּישׁ לֵית לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי שמעון's position from step 16 using a different פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's ruling that an אונן may eat ביכורים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah requires joy with ביכורים, and an אונן cannot be joyful, so he should be forbidden even without the הקש.

steps.title: Joy refers to the season, not the person
steps.stepSummary: The word שמחה teaches the proper time to bring ביכורים, the joyous harvest season. It does not require the owner to be personally happy. A משנה about the times of bringing and reciting supports this.
steps.simpleTranslation: That verse comes to teach the time of joy. As we learned in a משנה: from עצרת until סוכות, a person brings ביכורים and recites the passage. From סוכות until חנוכה, he brings them but does not recite.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that "ושמחת" sets the time period for ביכורים. It does not require the owner to feel joy, so an אונן is not excluded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full ritual, bringing and reciting, applies only from עצרת to סוכות, the season of joy. After סוכות the joyous season has ended, so the person brings the fruits but does not recite. This shows that "שמחה" defines a season, so רבי שמעון's ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The season of joy (the harvest period)

steps.whatToRemember: רבנן: ביכורים are like מעשר, so they are forbidden to an אונן. רבי שמעון: ביכורים are called תרומה, so they are permitted. For רבי שמעון, "ושמחת" sets the season (עצרת to סוכות), not the owner's personal mood. This is why, for רבי יוסי הגלילי, "לחם עוני" does not exclude ביכורים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer completes the support for step 13. Once ביכורים are permitted to an אונן, רבי יוסי הגלילי needs "בכל מושבותיכם" to exclude them from the מצוה of מצה.

phrases.english: That verse comes to teach the time of joy,
phrases.notes: It refers to a season, not to the person's feelings.

phrases.english: as we learned in a mishnah: from Shavuot until Sukkot,
one brings the first fruits and recites the passage;
from Sukkot until Chanukah,
one brings them but does not recite.
phrases.notes: The joyous season is over, so the full ritual no longer applies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the verse: שמחה refers to a season, not to the person's state of mind.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "ושמחת" requires the owner to be personally joyful, which would exclude an אונן.
steps.terutzMaskana: "ושמחת" sets the joyous season for ביכורים (עצרת to סוכות), so an אונן may still eat them according to רבי שמעון.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי שמעון's permission for an אונן to eat ביכורים stands.

steps.title: Poor man's bread excludes boiled מצה and large cakes
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the words "לחם עוני" rule out חלוט (boiled מצה) and אשישה (a large, fancy cake).
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: "Poor man's bread" comes to exclude boiled מצה and a large cake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a ברייתא about which kinds of מצה do not count for the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah calls מצה "לחם עוני", poor man's bread. The ברייתא learns from this that מצה made in a luxurious way does not count. Two examples are given: מצה boiled in hot water after baking (חלוט), and מצה baked as a big fancy cake (אשישה).

keyTerms.meaning: Poor man's bread, the Torah's name for מצה
Dough or מצה scalded or boiled in hot water

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
"Poor man's bread" excludes boiled [matza] and a large cake.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא states its rule first, then explains it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, separate from the אונן and ביכורים discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Boiled מצה and large-cake מצה do not count for the מצוה of eating מצה, because of the words "לחם עוני".

steps.title: Maybe only coarse bread is allowed
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא raises a possible mistake: maybe "poor man's bread" means only coarse, low-quality bread counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think a person only fulfills his obligation with coarse bread?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible wrong conclusion (a "יכול") so that it can correct it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If "לחם עוני" means poor man's bread, maybe the מצה must be made from cheap, rough flour like a poor person eats. This is only a passing thought, and the ברייתא is about to reject it.

keyTerms.meaning: "I might have thought", a possible mistaken idea
His obligation, meaning fulfilling the מצוה
Coarse bread made from rough, unsifted flour

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל לֹא יֵצֵא אָדָם יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ
phrases.english: I might think a person does not fulfill his obligation
except with coarse bread?

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל לֹא יֵצֵא אָדָם יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests how far the rule of step 19 should go.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does "לחם עוני" require low-quality, coarse flour?

steps.title: Even the finest מצה is allowed
steps.stepSummary: The repeated word "מצות" teaches that fine-flour מצה counts too, even מצות as fine as שלמה המלך's.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says "מצות", "מצות", which widens the rule, so even מצות like those of שלמה are fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question from step 20: no, fancy flour is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah uses the word "מצות" more than once, and that extra wording includes more kinds of מצה (ריבה). So the quality of the flour does not matter. Even the finest מצה, like a king would eat, counts.

keyTerms.meaning: It widened the rule to include more cases
The fancy מצות of שלמה המלך, made of the finest flour

phrases.english: The verse states: "matzot," "matzot": it amplified,
and even [matzot] like the matzot of Solomon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the idea raised in step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Fine flour is allowed. The repeated "מצות" includes even the most luxurious מצה.

steps.title: So poor man's bread only rules out boiled מצה and large cakes
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא wraps up: "לחם עוני" only excludes חלוט and אשישה, not fine flour.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the verse say "poor man's bread"? To exclude boiled מצה and a large cake.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks what "לחם עוני" still teaches, and repeats its original rule as the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since fancy flour is allowed, "לחם עוני" cannot be about flour quality. It is about how the מצה is made. Boiling it or baking it as a big rich cake changes it from plain bread, so those do not count.

keyTerms.meaning: Why then does the verse say

steps.whatToRemember: Flour quality does not matter for מצה. What disqualifies it is a fancy way of making it: boiling it (חלוט) or baking it as a large cake (אשישה).
steps.confusionAlert: "Poor man's bread" does NOT mean the flour must be cheap. Even the finest flour is fine. It only rules out these two special ways of preparing the מצה.

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן, מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״לֶחֶם עוֹנִי״
phrases.english: If so, why does the verse state "poor man's bread"?
To exclude boiled [matza] and a large cake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings steps 20-21 back to the opening rule of step 19 and confirms it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: "לחם עוני" excludes only חלוט and אשישה. Fine flour is permitted.

steps.title: How do we know אשישה means something fancy?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for proof that the word אשישה refers to something important or luxurious.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that this word אשישה is a term for something important?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how we know that אשישה means a fancy item, which is why it is excluded from "poor man's bread".
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא assumed that אשישה is not "poor" bread. The גמרא wants a source showing that the word really refers to something important (חשיבות).

keyTerms.meaning: How is it implied, how do we know

phrases.english: And from where is it implied
that this [word] ashisha is a term of importance?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word the ברייתא used.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that אשישה means something important or luxurious.

steps.title: דוד המלך handed out אשישה at a celebration
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in שמואל ב tells how דוד המלך gave each person bread, an אשפר, and an אשישה at his celebration.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: "He handed out to all the people, all of Israel, men and women, to each one a loaf of bread, an אשפר, and an אשישה."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק about דוד המלך's festive gifts when he brought the ארון to ירושלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A king gives fine gifts at a royal celebration, and אשישה is listed among these gifts. The proof is completed in the next step, where רב חנן בר אבא explains that אשישה is a large cake made from a sixth of an איפה. That shows it is a rich, important item.

keyTerms.meaning: A gift mentioned in the פסוק, explained in the next step

phrases.english: As it is written: "And he distributed to all the people,
to the whole multitude of Israel,
both men and women,
to each one a loaf of bread,
and an eshpar and an ashisha, etc." (II Samuel 6:19)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אשישה was one of the royal gifts דוד המלך gave at his celebration, so it is something important.

steps.title: רב חנן בר אבא explains אשפר and אשישה
steps.stepSummary: רב חנן בר אבא explains that אשפר is a sixth of an ox, and אשישה is a cake made from a sixth of an איפה of flour.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חנן בר אבא said: אשפר means one-sixth of an ox. אשישה means one-sixth of an איפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רב חנן בר אבא's explanation of the words in the פסוק, which shows how large and rich these gifts were.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads אשפר as "אחד מששה בפר", one of six in an ox, meaning a big piece of meat. He reads אשישה as a cake from one-sixth of an איפה of flour (the word sounds like שש, six). This fits the idea that אשישה is a large, important cake.

keyTerms.meaning: A large dry measure for flour

phrases.english: And Rav Ḥanan bar Abba said:
"Eshpar" is one-sixth of an ox;
"ashisha" is one-sixth of an eipha.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the words of the פסוק quoted in step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אשישה is a large cake made from one-sixth of an איפה of flour, and אשפר is one-sixth of an ox.

steps.title: שמואל says אשישה is a jug of wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that שמואל disagrees: for him, אשישה means a jug of wine, based on a פסוק in הושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: This disagrees with שמואל, because שמואל said: אשישה is a jug of wine, as it is written: "And those who love jugs of grapes."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that שמואל explains the word אשישה differently from רב חנן בר אבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל, the אשישה in דוד's gifts was a jug of wine, not a cake. He proves this from הושע, where "אשישי ענבים" refers to containers of grape wine. The גמרא only notes that he disagrees. It does not explain how his reading fits the ברייתא's use of אשישה for a large cake.

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Shmuel,
as Shmuel said: "Ashisha" is a jug of wine,
as it is written: "And those who love jugs of grapes" (Hosea 3:1).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing explanation of the word that רב חנן בר אבא explained in step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to שמואל, the אשישה in the פסוק is a jug of wine.

steps.title: בית שמאי: no baking thick bread on פסח
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא begins: בית שמאי rule that thick bread may not be baked on יום טוב of פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: One may not bake thick bread on יום טוב of פסח. These are the words of בית שמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new ברייתא. This line gives בית שמאי's view and sets up a disagreement that continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Thick dough takes longer to bake through, so it might become חמץ before it is fully baked. So בית שמאי forbid it on פסח. The words "דברי בית שמאי" signal that another opinion is coming.

keyTerms.meaning: The words of (marks whose opinion this is)

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One may not bake thick bread
(on the Festival) on Passover;
these are the words of Beit Shammai,

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין אוֹפִין פַּת עָבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא on a related topic: how מצה may be baked on פסח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: thick bread may not be baked on יום טוב of פסח (because it might become חמץ).
